title: API
body:
*Application Programming Interface* — a defined contract for how one piece of software talks to another. On the web it usually means a set of [[Endpoint]]s a server exposes, which a [[Client]] calls over [[HTTP]] and gets [[JSON]] back from.

The reason it matters is decoupling: the contract is the only thing either side depends on, so the backend can be rewritten entirely — new language, new database, new servers — and nothing on the frontend has to change as long as the endpoints keep behaving the same. It's the boundary between the [[Frontend]] and the [[Backend]].

In practice you consume one with [[Fetch]], and you build one with [[Express]]. Design conventions are covered in [[REST]], and the full analogy walkthrough is in [[REST APIs]].
